+++ b/assets/js/schedule_window.js
@@ -0,0 +1,177 @@
+// Fixed slot geometry keeps scroll position independent of materialized cells.
+const SLOT_WIDTH = 80
+const NAME_WIDTH = 148
+const BUFFER = 8
+const MAX_COLUMNS = 128
+
+export function desiredWindow(scrollLeft, clientWidth, total) {
+  if (total <= 0) return {start: 0, count: 0, first: 0}
+  const first = Math.max(0, Math.min(total - 1, Math.floor(scrollLeft / SLOT_WIDTH)))
+  const visible = Math.ceil(Math.max(clientWidth - NAME_WIDTH, 0) / SLOT_WIDTH) + 1
+  const count = Math.min(total, MAX_COLUMNS, visible + BUFFER * 2)
+  const start = Math.min(Math.max(first - BUFFER, 0), total - count)
+  return {start, count, first}
+}
+
+export function createScheduleWindowHook(browserLatency) {
+  return {
+    mounted() {
+      this._generation = 0
+      this._eventRefs = []
+      this.readMetadata()
+      this._eventRefs.push(this.handleEvent("scroll-to-schedule", ({schedule_id}) => {
+        const index = this._slots.findIndex(slot => String(slot[2]) === String(schedule_id))
+        if (index >= 0) this.moveTo(index * SLOT_WIDTH)
+      }))
+      this._eventRefs.push(this.handleEvent("restore-schedule-focus", ({cell_id, index}) => {
+        const left = this._modalScrollLeft ?? index * SLOT_WIDTH
+        this._modalScrollLeft = null
+        this._focusPending = cell_id
+        this.moveTo(left)
+      }))
+      this.connect()
+      const today = Number(this.el.dataset.todayIndex)
+      if (today >= 0 && today < this._slots.length) this.moveTo(today * SLOT_WIDTH)
+    },
+
+    beforeUpdate() { this._savedScrollLeft = this.el.scrollLeft },
+
+    updated() {
+      if (this._savedScrollLeft != null) this.el.scrollLeft = this._savedScrollLeft
+      this._savedScrollLeft = null
+      this.readMetadata()
+      const modalOpen = !!document.getElementById("gantt-rotation-modal")
+      if (modalOpen && !this._modalOpen) this._modalScrollLeft = this.el.scrollLeft
+      this._modalOpen = modalOpen
+      this.scheduleFrame()
+    },
+
+    disconnected() { this.disconnect() },
+    reconnected() { this.connect() },
+    destroyed() {
+      this.disconnect()
+      for (const ref of this._eventRefs || []) this.removeHandleEvent?.(ref)
+      this._eventRefs = []
+    },
+
+    connect() {
+      if (this._connected) return
+      this._connected = true
+      this._onScroll = () => this.scheduleFrame()
+      this._onResize = () => this.scheduleFrame()
+      this.el.addEventListener("scroll", this._onScroll, {passive: true})
+      if (typeof ResizeObserver !== "undefined") {
+        this._observer = new ResizeObserver(this._onResize)
+        this._observer.observe(this.el)
+      } else {
+        window.addEventListener("resize", this._onResize)
+      }
+      this.scheduleFrame()
+    },
+
+    disconnect() {
+      this._connected = false
+      this._generation++
+      browserLatency.cancelHook(this)
+      if (this._frame != null) cancelAnimationFrame(this._frame)
+      this._frame = null
+      this._inflight = null
+      this._ackedYear = null
+      this.el.removeEventListener("scroll", this._onScroll)
+      this._observer?.disconnect()
+      this._observer = null
+      window.removeEventListener("resize", this._onResize)
+    },
+
+    readMetadata() {
+      const metadata = this.el.dataset.slotMetadata
+      if (this._metadata !== metadata) {
+        this._metadata = metadata
+        this._slots = JSON.parse(metadata || "[]")
+        this._ackedYear = null
+      }
+      this.yearEl = document.getElementById("gantt-year-indicator")
+    },
+
+    moveTo(left) {
+      this.el.scrollLeft = Math.max(0, left)
+      this.scheduleFrame()
+    },
+
+    scheduleFrame() {
+      if (!this._connected || this._frame != null) return
+      this._frame = requestAnimationFrame(() => {
+        this._frame = null
+        if (!this._connected) return
+        this.updateYear()
+        this.updateActivePill()
+        this.updateCohortVisibility()
+        this.restoreFocus()
+        this.requestWindow()
+      })
+    },
+
+    visibleRange() {
+      return desiredWindow(this.el.scrollLeft, this.el.clientWidth, this._slots.length)
+    },
+
+    requestWindow() {
+      if (this._inflight || !this._slots.length) return
+      const desired = this.visibleRange()
+      const year = this._slots[desired.first][1]
+      const start = Number(this.el.dataset.windowStart)
+      const finish = start + Number(this.el.dataset.windowCount)
+      const visibleEnd = Math.min(this._slots.length,
+        desired.first + Math.ceil(Math.max(this.el.clientWidth - NAME_WIDTH, 0) / SLOT_WIDTH) + 1)
+      const nearLeft = start > 0 && desired.first < start + BUFFER / 2
+      const nearRight = finish < this._slots.length && visibleEnd > finish - BUFFER / 2
+      if (!nearLeft && !nearRight && desired.first >= start && visibleEnd <= finish && year === this._ackedYear) return
+      const generation = this._generation
+      this._inflight = desired
+      browserLatency.measureHookEvent(this, "schedule", "update_window", desired, () => {
+        if (!this._connected || generation !== this._generation) return
+        this._inflight = null
+        this._ackedYear = year
+        this.scheduleFrame()
+      })
+    },
+
+    restoreFocus() {
+      if (!this._focusPending) return
+      const target = document.getElementById(`gantt-pill-${this._focusPending}`) || this.el
+      this._focusPending = null
+      target.focus({preventScroll: true})
+    },
+
+    updateYear() {
+      const slot = this._slots[this.visibleRange().first]
+      if (this.yearEl && slot) this.yearEl.textContent = String(slot[0])
+    },
+
+    updateActivePill() {
+      const slot = this._slots[this.visibleRange().first]
+      const active = slot && String(slot[2])
+      document.querySelectorAll("[data-schedule-pill]").forEach(pill => {
+        const selected = pill.dataset.schedulePill === active
+        pill.classList.toggle("bg-blue-600", selected)
+        pill.classList.toggle("text-white", selected)
+        pill.classList.toggle("bg-gray-100", !selected)
+        pill.classList.toggle("text-gray-700", !selected)
+        pill.classList.toggle("dark:bg-gray-800", !selected)
+        pill.classList.toggle("dark:text-gray-200", !selected)
+      })
+    },
+
+    updateCohortVisibility() {
+      const first = this.visibleRange().first
+      const count = Math.ceil(Math.max(this.el.clientWidth - NAME_WIDTH, 0) / SLOT_WIDTH) + 1
+      const years = this._slots.slice(first, first + count).map(slot => slot[1])
+      if (!years.length) return
+      const min = Math.min(...years), max = Math.max(...years) + 3
+      this.el.querySelectorAll("tr[data-cohort-graduation-year]").forEach(row => {
+        const year = Number(row.dataset.cohortGraduationYear)
+        row.classList.toggle("hidden", year < min || year > max)
+      })
+    }
+  }
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,84 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Optional Linux-container rehearsal. Build the exact scp-action v0.1.7 image
+# first, then pass its local image name. No external network or real credentials.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+test "$#" -eq 1 || { echo 'usage: bash test/deploy/private_transfer_test.sh LOCAL_SCP_ACTION_IMAGE' >&2; exit 1; }
+image=$1
+root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)
+scratch=$(mktemp -d)
+volume="phase0-private-transfer-test-$$-$RANDOM"
+trap 'docker volume rm -f "$volume" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; rm -rf "$scratch"' EXIT
+
+test "$(docker image inspect "$image" --format '{{.Config.User}}')" = '1000:1000'
+docker volume create "$volume" >/dev/null
+
+# Execute the workflow's actual bounded handoff and cleanup, rather than a
+# duplicate implementation. The Ruby suite checks their order for both jobs.
+ruby - "$root/.github/workflows/deploy.yml" "$scratch" <<'RUBY'
+require 'yaml'
+jobs = YAML.load_file(ARGV[0]).fetch('jobs')
+directory = ARGV[1]
+%w[staging deploy].each do |name|
+  steps = jobs.fetch(name).fetch('steps')
+  render = steps.index { |step| step['run'].to_s.include?('runtime_config.rb render') }
+  upload = steps.index { |step| step.dig('with', 'source') == 'runtime-config/runtime.json' }
+  commands = steps[render...upload].flat_map { |step| step['run'].to_s.lines }
+  handoff = commands.find { |line| line.include?('chown') }
+  abort "missing private ownership handoff in #{name}" unless handoff
+  abort "unbounded ownership handoff in #{name}" unless handoff.strip == 'sudo chown 1000:1000 runtime-config runtime-config/runtime.json'
+  cleanup = steps.find { |step| step['name'] == 'Remove private local configuration' }.fetch('run')
+  abort "unsafe private cleanup in #{name}" unless cleanup.strip == 'sudo rm -f runtime-config/runtime.json'
+  File.write(File.join(directory, "#{name}-handoff.sh"), handoff)
+  File.write(File.join(directory, "#{name}-cleanup.sh"), cleanup)
+end
+File.write(File.join(directory, 'runtime.json'), '{"ACCESS_PASSWORD":"synthetic-transfer-sentinel"}')
+RUBY
+
+container_root() {
+  docker run --rm --network none --user 0 \
+    -v "$volume:/github/workspace" -v "$scratch:/checks:ro" \
+    -w /github/workspace --entrypoint /bin/sh "$image" -c "$1"
+}
+
+action_archive() {
+  docker run --rm --network none -v "$volume:/github/workspace:ro" \
+    -w /github/workspace -e INPUT_HOST=127.0.0.1 -e INPUT_PORT=1 \
+    -e INPUT_USERNAME=synthetic -e INPUT_PASSWORD=synthetic-public-fixture \
+    -e INPUT_SOURCE=runtime-config/runtime.json -e INPUT_TARGET=/tmp/synthetic-target/ \
+    -e INPUT_STRIP_COMPONENTS=1 "$image"
+}
+
+for job in staging deploy; do
+  container_root 'mkdir -p runtime-config; cp /checks/runtime.json runtime-config/runtime.json; chown 1001:1001 runtime-config runtime-config/runtime.json; chmod 700 runtime-config; chmod 600 runtime-config/runtime.json'
+
+  # Reproduce the actual Actions runner UID versus the pinned image's UID.
+  if action_archive >"$scratch/before.log" 2>&1; then
+    echo 'unexpected successful network-disabled baseline' >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  rg -q 'tar: empty archive' "$scratch/before.log"
+
+  # Only sudo is adapted: the disposable helper already runs as root. chown,
+  # paths and private modes are the real workflow operations on a Linux volume.
+  container_root "sudo() { \"\$@\"; }; . /checks/$job-handoff.sh"
+  container_root 'test "$(stat -c %u:%g runtime-config)" = 1000:1000; test "$(stat -c %u:%g runtime-config/runtime.json)" = 1000:1000; test "$(stat -c %a runtime-config)" = 700; test "$(stat -c %a runtime-config/runtime.json)" = 600'
+
+  if action_archive >"$scratch/after.log" 2>&1; then
+    echo 'unexpected network access in isolated action rehearsal' >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  ! rg -q 'tar: empty archive|Permission denied' "$scratch/after.log"
+  rg -q 'connection refused' "$scratch/after.log"
+  ! rg -q 'synthetic-transfer-sentinel' "$scratch/before.log" "$scratch/after.log"
+
+  # The actual image user must be able to archive the exact private bytes and
+  # retain the source file's mode, independently of the expected SSH refusal.
+  docker run --rm --network none -v "$volume:/github/workspace:ro" \
+    -w /github/workspace --entrypoint /bin/sh "$image" \
+    -c 'tar -czf /tmp/private.tar.gz runtime-config/runtime.json; test "$(tar -tzf /tmp/private.tar.gz)" = runtime-config/runtime.json; tar -xzf /tmp/private.tar.gz -C /tmp; cmp runtime-config/runtime.json /tmp/runtime-config/runtime.json; test "$(stat -c %a /tmp/runtime-config/runtime.json)" = 600'
+
+  container_root "sudo() { \"\$@\"; }; . /checks/$job-cleanup.sh; test ! -e runtime-config/runtime.json"
+done
+
+echo 'Private transfer rehearsal passed for staging and deploy (isolated Linux UID handoff; no network).'

+#!/usr/bin/env ruby
+# frozen_string_literal: true
+
+# External-process protocol fixture. It never contacts PostgreSQL or object storage.
+require 'base64'
+require 'digest'
+require 'json'
+require 'fileutils'
+require 'time'
+
+state_path = ENV.fetch('BACKUP_STUB_STATE')
+state = JSON.parse(File.read(state_path))
+name = File.basename($PROGRAM_NAME)
+event_path = ENV.fetch('BACKUP_STUB_EVENTS')
+event = lambda do |sql = nil, extra = {}|
+  File.open(event_path, 'a') do |file|
+    file.puts(JSON.generate({command: name, argv: ARGV, sql: sql, pid: Process.pid,
+      environment: ENV.select { |key, _| key.start_with?('AWS', 'PG') }}.merge(extra)))
+  end
+end
+fail_private = lambda do
+  warn state.fetch('private_sentinel')
+  exit 17
+end
+
+if state['hang_command'] == name
+  event.call
+  child = fork { loop { sleep 1 } }
+  File.write(ENV.fetch('BACKUP_STUB_CHILD'), child.to_s)
+  loop { sleep 1 }
+end
+fail_private.call if state['fail_command'] == name
+
+case name
+when 'runuser'
+  event.call
+  separator = ARGV.index('--')
+  abort('fixed runuser protocol required') unless separator
+  exec(*ARGV[(separator + 1)..])
+when 'psql'
+  respond = lambda do |sql|
+    event.call(sql)
+    if sql.include?('recovery:cluster') || sql.include?('backup:cluster')
+      puts JSON.generate(cluster_identifier: state.fetch('cluster'), in_recovery: state.fetch('in_recovery', false))
+    elsif sql.include?('recovery:snapshot') || sql.include?('backup:snapshot')
+      File.write(ENV.fetch('BACKUP_STUB_EXPORTER'), Process.pid.to_s)
+      puts '00000003-0000001B-1'
+    elsif sql.include?('recovery:inventory') || sql.include?('backup:inventory')
+      puts JSON.generate(state.fetch('inventory'))
+    elsif sql.include?('recovery:table') || sql.include?('backup:table')
+      puts state.fetch('raw_rows')
+    end
+    STDOUT.flush
+  end
+  index = ARGV.index('-c') || ARGV.index('--command')
+  if index
+    respond.call(ARGV[index + 1])
+  else
+    buffer = +''
+    STDIN.each_line do |line|
+      buffer << line
+      if line.include?(';')
+        respond.call(buffer)
+        buffer.clear
+      end
+    end
+    respond.call(buffer) unless buffer.empty?
+  end
+when 'pg_dump'
+  lock = File.open(state.fetch('lock_path'), File::RDWR)
+  lock_held = !lock.flock(File::LOCK_EX | File::LOCK_NB)
+  lock.flock(File::LOCK_UN) unless lock_held
+  event.call(nil, lock_held: lock_held)
+  Process.kill(0, Integer(File.read(ENV.fetch('BACKUP_STUB_EXPORTER'))))
+  if state['dump_excess_bytes']
+    STDOUT.write('x' * state.fetch('dump_excess_bytes'))
+  else
+    STDOUT.write(state.fetch('dump'))
+  end
+  exit(state.fetch('dump_exit', 0))
+when 'gpg'
+  event.call
+  abort('streaming encryption required') unless ARGV.include?('--encrypt')
+  output_index = ARGV.index('--output') || ARGV.index('-o')
+  output = output_index && ARGV[output_index + 1]
+  input = STDIN.read
+  encrypted = "SYNTHETIC-CIPHER\n" + Base64.strict_encode64(input)
+  output ? File.binwrite(output, encrypted) : STDOUT.write(encrypted)
+when 'aws'
+  service = ARGV.index('s3api')
+  abort('s3api required') unless service
+  operation = ARGV[service + 1]
+  value = lambda do |key|
+    index = ARGV.index(key)
+    index && ARGV[index + 1]
+  end
+  key = value.call('--key')
+  event.call(nil, operation: operation, key: key)
+  if state['fail_aws'] == operation || state['fail_key_suffix'] && key&.end_with?(state['fail_key_suffix'])
+    fail_private.call
+  end
+  objects = state.fetch('objects')
+  case operation
+  when 'list-objects-v2'
+    prefix = value.call('--prefix').to_s
+    matching = objects.keys.select { |candidate| candidate.start_with?(prefix) }.sort
+    maximum = value.call('--max-keys').to_i
+    maximum = 1000 if maximum.zero?
+    limited = matching.take(maximum)
+    puts JSON.generate(Contents: limited.map { |candidate| {Key: candidate, Size: Base64.strict_decode64(objects.fetch(candidate).fetch('body')).bytesize} }, IsTruncated: matching.length > maximum)
+  when 'put-object'
+    body = File.binread(value.call('--body'))
+    version = state.fetch('versioned', true) ? "version-#{objects.length + 1}" : nil
+    objects[key] = {'body' => Base64.strict_encode64(body), 'version_id' => version, 'last_modified' => Time.now.utc.iso8601}
+    File.write(state_path, JSON.generate(state))
+    puts JSON.generate(VersionId: version, ETag: 'deliberately-not-a-content-sha')
+  when 'get-object', 'head-object'
+    object = objects[key]
+    fail_private.call unless object
+    requested = value.call('--version-id')
+    fail_private.call if requested && requested != object['version_id']
+    body = Base64.strict_decode64(object.fetch('body'))
+    body += 'corrupted-readback' if state['corrupt_get_suffix'] && key.end_with?(state['corrupt_get_suffix'])
+    body = 'x' * state['get_excess_bytes'] if state['get_excess_bytes']
+    File.binwrite(ARGV.last, body) if operation == 'get-object'
+    puts JSON.generate(VersionId: object['version_id'], ContentLength: body.bytesize,
+      LastModified: object.fetch('last_modified'), ETag: 'deliberately-not-a-content-sha')
+  else
+    abort("forbidden storage mutation #{operation}")
+  end
+else
+  abort('unexpected executable')
+end

+        kind = "float" if (end - start).days == 6 else "weekend" if start.weekday() == 5 else "weekday"
+        slots.append(dict(column=column, start=start, end=end, kind=kind))
+    names, grid = {}, {}
+    for row in rows[2:]:
+        if not row or not row[0].startswith(tuple(f"R{y}-" for y in range(1, 5))):
+            continue
+        code = row[0].strip()
+        if code in names:
+            raise ValueError("Duplicate position code")
+        names[code] = row[1]
+        values = [row[s["column"]] if s["column"] < len(row) else "" for s in slots]
+        grid[code] = [value if value.strip().upper() == "FLOAT" else value.strip().upper() for value in values]
+    return Schedule(slots, names, grid, rows)
+
+
+def project_resident(slots, cells):
+    if len(slots) != len(cells):
+        raise ValueError("Wrong assignment count")
+    cells = [cell.strip().upper() for cell in cells]
+    shifts, float_dates = [], set()
+    by_start = {s["start"]: cell for s, cell in zip(slots, cells)}
+    by_end = {s["end"]: cell for s, cell in zip(slots, cells)}
+    for slot, rotation in zip(slots, cells):
+        if rotation not in KNOWN:
+            raise ValueError(f"Unknown rotation {rotation!r}")
+        start, end = slot["start"], slot["end"]
+        if rotation == "FLOAT":
+            float_dates.update(dates(start, end))
+            continue
+        if rotation in ABSENCE:
+            continue
+        canonical_weekday = start.weekday() == 0 and (end - start).days == 4
+        canonical_weekend = start.weekday() == 5 and (end - start).days == 1
+        if rotation == "NF" and canonical_weekday:
+            start, end = start - DAY, end - DAY
+        elif rotation == "HNF":
+            start -= DAY
+        elif rotation == "HWN":
+            end = start
+        elif rotation == "AMB" and canonical_weekday and by_start.get(end + DAY) == "SWN":
+            end -= DAY
+        elif rotation == "SWN" and canonical_weekend and by_end.get(start - DAY) == "AMB":
+            start, end = start - DAY, end - DAY
+        for shift_date in dates(start, end):
+            shifts.append(dict(date=shift_date, rotation=rotation, hours=12 if rotation in HOSPITAL else 8,
+                               night=rotation in NIGHTS))
+    return dict(shifts=sorted(shifts, key=lambda s: s["date"]), float_dates=float_dates)
+
+
+def weekend_key(shift):
+    day = shift["date"]
+    if day.weekday() >= 5 or (day.weekday() == 4 and shift["night"]):
+        return day + DAY * (5 - day.weekday())
+    return None
+
+
+def workload(projected):
+    weekends = [weekend_key(s) for s in projected["shifts"]]
+    return dict(night_shifts=sum(s["night"] for s in projected["shifts"]),
+                weekend_shifts=sum(key is not None for key in weekends),
+                weekends_worked=len({key for key in weekends if key is not None}))
+
+
+def duty_windows(projected, start, end):
+    hours = Counter()
+    for shift in projected["shifts"]:
+        hours[shift["date"]] += shift["hours"]
+    return [dict(start=day, hours=sum(hours[d] for d in dates(day, day + 27 * DAY)),
+                 complete=not any(d in projected["float_dates"] for d in dates(day, day + 27 * DAY)))
+            for day in dates(start, end - 27 * DAY)]
+
+
+def range_deviation(values):
+    if not values:
+        return 0, 0
+    return max(values) - min(values), sum(abs(len(values) * v - sum(values)) for v in values)
+
+
+def fairness_objective(workloads, education):
+    totals = [0] * 8
+    for year in range(1, 5):
+        codes = [c for c in workloads if c.startswith(f"R{year}-")]
+        for key, a, b in [("night_shifts", 0, 1), ("weekend_shifts", 2, 4), ("weekends_worked", 3, 5)]:
+            spread, deviation = range_deviation([workloads[c][key] for c in codes])
+            totals[a] += spread
+            totals[b] += deviation
+        labels = set().union(*(set(education.get(c, {})) for c in codes))
+        for label in labels:
+            spread, deviation = range_deviation([education.get(c, {}).get(label, 0) for c in codes])
+            totals[6] += spread
+            totals[7] += deviation
+    return tuple(totals)
+
+
+def education_target_deviation(education, targets):
+    result = 0
+    for year, target in targets.items():
+        codes = [c for c in education if c.startswith(f"R{year}-")]
+        for label in set(target).union(*(set(education[c]) for c in codes)):
+            result += abs(sum(education[c].get(label, 0) for c in codes) - len(codes) * target.get(label, 0))
+    return result
+
+
+def education_counts(schedule):
+    return {c: dict(Counter(cell for slot, cell in zip(schedule.slots, cells) if slot["kind"] == "weekday"))
+            for c, cells in schedule.grid.items()}
+
+
+def validate_schedule(schedule, baseline):
+    errors = []
+    expected = {f"R{y}-{n}" for y in range(1, 5) for n in range(1, 9)}
+    def error(constraint, **details):
+        errors.append(dict(constraint=constraint, **details))
+    if set(schedule.grid) != expected or set(schedule.names) != expected:
+        error("identities")
+        return errors
+    if schedule.names != baseline.names or schedule.names != SYNTHETIC_NAMES:
+        error("synthetic_names")

      TimingDoctestFixtures.source()

      for options <- [
            [batch_size: 0],
            [batch_size: 1001],
            [batch_size: -1],
            [batch_size: "1"],
            [batch_size: nil],
            [unknown: 1],
            [batch_size: 1, unknown: 1],
            :bad,
            %{batch_size: 1}
          ] do
        assert {:error, :invalid_batch_size} = Timings.backfill(options), inspect(options)
        assert {:error, :invalid_batch_size} = Backfill.run(options), inspect(options)
      end

      assert rows() == []
    end

    test "the default and bounds of the batch size are accepted" do
      TimingDoctestFixtures.source()
      assert {:ok, %{processed: 1}} = Timings.backfill()
      assert {:ok, %{processed: 0, unchanged: 1}} = Timings.backfill([])
      assert {:ok, %{processed: 0, unchanged: 1}} = Timings.backfill(batch_size: 1)
      assert {:ok, %{processed: 0, unchanged: 1}} = Timings.backfill(batch_size: 500)
      assert {:ok, %{processed: 0, unchanged: 1}} = Timings.backfill(batch_size: 1000)
    end

    test "a batch size of one walks every source across batches by stable id" do
      ctx = TimingDoctestFixtures.source()
      second = TimingDoctestFixtures.add_source(ctx, period: nil, date: next_day(ctx, 31))
      third = TimingDoctestFixtures.add_source(ctx, period: "Night", date: next_day(ctx, 29))

      assert {:ok, counts} = Timings.backfill(batch_size: 1)
      assert counts == %{processed: 3, period: 2, date_only: 1, unchanged: 0, conflicting: 0}

      assert Enum.map(rows(), & &1["original_source_id"]) ==
               Enum.sort([ctx.source.id, second.source.id, third.source.id])

      assert {:ok, %{processed: 0, unchanged: 3}} = Timings.backfill(batch_size: 2)
    end

    test "a batch whose source kind is outside csv and qgenda is rolled back" do
      ctx = TimingDoctestFixtures.source()
      TimingDoctestFixtures.add_source(ctx, source_kind: "custom", date: next_day(ctx, 31))
      original = legacy_rows()

      assert {:error, :unsupported_namespace} = Timings.backfill()
      assert rows() == []
      assert legacy_rows() == original
    end

    test "earlier batches remain when a later batch has an unsupported source kind" do
      ctx = TimingDoctestFixtures.source()
      TimingDoctestFixtures.add_source(ctx, source_kind: "custom", date: next_day(ctx, 31))
      original = legacy_rows()

      assert {:error, :unsupported_namespace} = Timings.backfill(batch_size: 1)
      assert [saved] = rows()
      assert saved["original_source_id"] == ctx.source.id
      assert legacy_rows() == original

      assert {:error, :unsupported_namespace} = Backfill.run(batch_size: 1)
      assert rows() == [saved]
    end

    test "an empty source table completes with zero counts" do
      assert Timings.backfill() ==
               {:ok, %{processed: 0, period: 0, date_only: 0, unchanged: 0, conflicting: 0}}
    end
  end

    test "source deletion releases the live reference while retaining original evidence" do
      ctx = TimingDoctestFixtures.source()
      assert {:ok, %{processed: 1}} = Timings.backfill()
      [before] = rows()

      Repo.delete!(ctx.source)

            end_date: Date.new!(ctx.schedule.academic_year + 1, 1, 3),
            rotation_type: :strong_gynecology
          }
        ])

      assert {:ok, %{processed: 2}} = Timings.backfill(batch_size: 1)
      assert legacy_rows() == original
      assert {:ok, %{processed: 0, unchanged: 2}} = Timings.backfill()
      assert legacy_rows() == original
    end

    test "the database rejects duplicate original evidence and inconsistent timing rows" do
      ctx = TimingDoctestFixtures.source()
      assert {:ok, %{processed: 1}} = Timings.backfill()
      [timing] = rows()

      assert_rejected(
        "INSERT INTO activity_source_timings (original_source_id, activity_source_id, namespace, source_date, precision, period, source_snapshot, input_digest, rule_version, policy, evidence_origin, inserted_at, updated_at) SELECT original_source_id, activity_source_id, namespace, source_date, precision, period, source_snapshot, input_digest, rule_version, policy, evidence_origin, inserted_at, updated_at FROM activity_source_timings WHERE id=$1",
        [timing["id"]]
      )

      assert_rejected("UPDATE activity_source_timings SET precision='exact' WHERE id=$1", [
        timing["id"]
      ])

      assert_rejected("UPDATE activity_source_timings SET period=NULL WHERE id=$1", [
        timing["id"]
      ])

      assert_rejected("UPDATE activity_source_timings SET period='Evening' WHERE id=$1", [
        timing["id"]
      ])

      assert_rejected(
        "UPDATE activity_source_timings SET starts_at=now(), ends_at=now() + interval '1 hour', time_zone='America/New_York' WHERE id=$1",
        [timing["id"]]
      )

      assert_rejected("UPDATE activity_source_timings SET namespace='other' WHERE id=$1", [
        timing["id"]
      ])

      assert_rejected("UPDATE activity_source_timings SET policy='guessed' WHERE id=$1", [
        timing["id"]
      ])

      assert_rejected("UPDATE activity_source_timings SET evidence_origin='bot' WHERE id=$1", [
        timing["id"]
      ])

      assert_rejected(
        "UPDATE activity_source_timings SET activity_source_id=original_source_id+1 WHERE id=$1",
        [timing["id"]]
      )

      assert rows() == [timing]
      assert Repo.get!(Activity, ctx.activity.id).period == "PM"
    end
  end

  describe "Release.backfill_timings/0" do
    test "the compiled release wrapper returns the backfill counts" do
      ctx = TimingDoctestFixtures.source()
      TimingDoctestFixtures.add_source(ctx, period: nil, date: next_day(ctx, 31))
      original = legacy_rows()

      assert Release.backfill_timings() ==
               {:ok, %{processed: 2, period: 1, date_only: 1, unchanged: 0, conflicting: 0}}

      assert Release.backfill_timings() ==
               {:ok, %{processed: 0, period: 0, date_only: 0, unchanged: 2, conflicting: 0}}

      assert length(rows()) == 2
      assert legacy_rows() == original
    end
  end

  defp next_day(ctx, day), do: Date.new!(ctx.schedule.academic_year, 12, day)

  defp rows do
    Repo.query!("SELECT to_jsonb(t) FROM activity_source_timings t ORDER BY id").rows
    |> Enum.map(&hd/1)
  end

  defp legacy_rows do
    Map.new(

        "detailed_activities",
        "detailed_activity_sources",
        "rotations"
      ],
      &{&1, Repo.query!("SELECT to_jsonb(t) FROM #{&1} t ORDER BY id").rows}
    )
  end

  defp assert_rejected(sql, params) do
    assert_raise Postgrex.Error, fn -> Repo.query!(sql, params, mode: :savepoint) end
  end
end

+defmodule ResidencySchedule.Timings do
+  @moduledoc """
+  Additive timing precision for saved source occurrences.
+
+  Each saved assignment records whether its source stated exact instants, a
+  part of the day or only a date. A period label never establishes hours, and
+  no stored date is adjusted. Existing importers, projections, calendar
+  exports and assistant queries remain authoritative and do not consult this
+  representation.
+  """
+  alias ResidencySchedule.Timings.{Backfill, Interpreter}
+
+  @doc """
+  Interprets stored timing facts without touching the database.
+
+      iex> {:ok, result} = ResidencySchedule.Timings.interpret(%{date: ~D[2026-12-30], period: "PM"})
+      iex> {result.source_date, result.precision, result.period}
+      {~D[2026-12-30], :period, "PM"}
+
+      iex> {:ok, result} = ResidencySchedule.Timings.interpret(%{date: ~D[2026-12-30], period: nil})
+      iex> {result.precision, result.policy}
+      {:date_only, "date_only"}
+  """
+  defdelegate interpret(facts), to: Interpreter
+
+  @doc """
+  Fills missing timing rows in restartable batches of 1–1000 (default 500).
+
+  Existing rows are never updated: rows whose stored facts or rule version
+  moved are reported as conflicting and retained, and reviewed/custom rows
+  stay unchanged. No source record is rewritten.

+      iex> {:ok, counts} = ResidencySchedule.Timings.backfill(batch_size: 1)
+      iex> {counts.processed, counts.period, counts.date_only, counts.unchanged}
+      {1, 1, 0, 0}
+  """

+defmodule ResidencySchedule.Timings.Backfill do
+  @moduledoc false
+  import Ecto.Query
+
+  alias ResidencySchedule.DetailedSchedules.{Activity, ActivitySource, ImportBatch}
+  alias ResidencySchedule.Repo
+  alias ResidencySchedule.ScheduleCache.Revision
+  alias ResidencySchedule.Timings.{Interpreter, Timing}
+
+  @rule_version "legacy_timing_v1"
+
+  @doc """
+  Records missing timing precision for saved sources from stored facts only.
+
+      iex> _ctx = ResidencySchedule.TimingDoctestFixtures.source()
+      iex> {:ok, counts} = ResidencySchedule.Timings.Backfill.run(batch_size: 1)
+      iex> {counts.processed, counts.period, counts.conflicting}
+      {1, 1, 0}
+  """
+  def run(options) do
+    with {:ok, size} <- batch_size(options) do
+      fill_pages(0, size, counts())
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp counts do
+    %{processed: 0, period: 0, date_only: 0, unchanged: 0, conflicting: 0}
+  end
+
+  defp batch_size(options) when is_list(options) do
+    if Keyword.keyword?(options) and Enum.all?(Keyword.keys(options), &(&1 == :batch_size)) do
+      case Keyword.get(options, :batch_size, 500) do
+        size when is_integer(size) and size in 1..1000 -> {:ok, size}
+        _ -> {:error, :invalid_batch_size}
+      end
+    else
+      {:error, :invalid_batch_size}
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp batch_size(_options), do: {:error, :invalid_batch_size}
+
+  defp fill_pages(after_id, size, total) do
+    ids =
+      ActivitySource
+      |> where([source], source.id > ^after_id)
+      |> order_by([source], source.id)
+      |> limit(^size)
+      |> select([source], source.id)
+      |> Repo.all()
+
+    case ids do
+      [] -> {:ok, total}
+      _ -> fill_next(ids, size, total)
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp fill_next(ids, size, total) do
+    case Repo.transaction(fn -> fill_page(ids) end) do
+      {:ok, page} ->
+        updated = Map.merge(total, page, fn _key, previous, value -> previous + value end)
+        fill_pages(List.last(ids), size, updated)
+
+      {:error, reason} ->
+        {:error, reason}
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp fill_page(ids) do
+    Revision.lock()
+
+    ids
+    |> source_rows()
+    |> Enum.reduce(counts(), &fill_source/2)
+  end
+
+  defp source_rows(ids) do
+    from(source in ActivitySource,
+      join: activity in Activity,
+      on: activity.id == source.activity_id,
+      join: batch in ImportBatch,
+      on: batch.id == source.batch_id,
+      where: source.id in ^ids,
+      order_by: source.id,
+      lock: "FOR UPDATE",
+      select: %{source: source, activity: activity, batch: batch}
+    )
+    |> Repo.all()
+  end
+
+  defp fill_source(row, totals) do
+    namespace = validate_namespace(row.batch)
+
+    existing =
+      Timing
+      |> where([timing], timing.original_source_id == ^row.source.id)
+      |> lock("FOR UPDATE")
+      |> Repo.one()
+
+    cond do
+      is_nil(existing) -> fill_missing(row, namespace, totals)
+      existing.evidence_origin != "legacy_code" -> increment(totals, :unchanged)
+      true -> retained_result(existing, row, totals)
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp validate_namespace(%ImportBatch{source_kind: kind}) when kind in ["csv", "qgenda"],
+    do: kind
+
+  defp validate_namespace(_batch), do: Repo.rollback(:unsupported_namespace)
+
+  defp retained_result(existing, row, totals) do
+    if existing.rule_version == @rule_version and
+         existing.input_digest == input_digest(source_snapshot(row.activity)),
+       do: increment(totals, :unchanged),
+       else: increment(totals, :conflicting)
+  end
+
+  defp fill_missing(row, namespace, totals) do
+    case Interpreter.interpret(%{date: row.activity.date, period: row.activity.period}) do
+      {:ok, result} ->
+        insert_timing(row, namespace, result)
+        totals |> increment(:processed) |> increment(result.precision)
+
+      {:error, :unsupported_period} ->
+        increment(totals, :conflicting)
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp insert_timing(row, namespace, result) do
+    snapshot = source_snapshot(row.activity)
+
+    Repo.insert!(%Timing{
+      original_source_id: row.source.id,
+      activity_source_id: row.source.id,
+      namespace: namespace,
+      source_date: result.source_date,
+      precision: Atom.to_string(result.precision),
+      period: result.period,
+      starts_at: result.starts_at,
+      ends_at: result.ends_at,
+      time_zone: result.time_zone,
+      source_snapshot: snapshot,
+      input_digest: input_digest(snapshot),
+      rule_version: result.rule_version,
+      policy: result.policy,
+      evidence_origin: "legacy_code"
+    })
+  end
+
+  defp source_snapshot(%Activity{} = activity) do
+    %{
+      "date" => Date.to_iso8601(activity.date),
+      "raw_task" => activity.raw_task,
+      "period" => activity.period
+    }
+  end
+
+  defp input_digest(snapshot) do
+    {snapshot, @rule_version}
+    |> :erlang.term_to_binary([:deterministic])
+    |> then(&:crypto.hash(:sha256, &1))
+    |> Base.encode16(case: :lower)
+  end
+
+  defp increment(counts, key), do: Map.update!(counts, key, &(&1 + 1))
+end

+defmodule ResidencySchedule.Timings.Interpreter do
+  @moduledoc """
+  Pure interpretation of how precisely one source occurrence states its time.
+
+  The caller's date is kept literally; a period label never establishes hours
+  and instants are only accepted as supplied, in one zone, with the end after
+  the start. Nothing here reads or writes the database.
+  """
+
+  @rule_version "legacy_timing_v1"
+  @periods ["AM", "PM", "Day", "Night"]
+
+  @doc """
+  Interprets stored timing facts into one precision outcome.
+
+      iex> {:ok, result} =
+      ...>   ResidencySchedule.Timings.Interpreter.interpret(%{date: ~D[2026-12-30], period: "PM"})
+      iex> {result.precision, result.period, result.policy, result.starts_at}
+      {:period, "PM", "stored_period", nil}
+
+      iex> ResidencySchedule.Timings.Interpreter.interpret(%{date: ~D[2026-12-30], period: "Evening"})
+      {:error, :unsupported_period}
+  """
+  def interpret(facts) when is_map(facts) do
+    with {:ok, date} <- fetch_date(facts) do
+      facts
+      |> instants()
+      |> interpret_shape(date, Map.get(facts, :period))
+    end
+  end
+
+  def interpret(_facts), do: {:error, :invalid_date}
+
+  defp fetch_date(%{date: %Date{} = date}), do: {:ok, date}
+  defp fetch_date(_facts), do: {:error, :invalid_date}
+
+  defp instants(facts), do: {Map.get(facts, :starts_at), Map.get(facts, :ends_at)}
+
+  defp interpret_shape({nil, nil}, date, nil), do: {:ok, date_only(date)}
+
+  defp interpret_shape({nil, nil}, date, period) when period in @periods,
+    do: {:ok, stored_period(date, period)}
+
+  defp interpret_shape({nil, nil}, _date, _period), do: {:error, :unsupported_period}
+
+  defp interpret_shape({starts_at, ends_at}, date, nil) do
+    if exact_instants?(starts_at, ends_at),
+      do: {:ok, exact(date, starts_at, ends_at)},
+      else: {:error, :invalid_instants}
+  end
+
+  defp interpret_shape(_instants, _date, _period), do: {:error, :invalid_instants}
+
+  defp exact_instants?(%DateTime{} = starts_at, %DateTime{} = ends_at) do
+    starts_at.time_zone == ends_at.time_zone and DateTime.compare(starts_at, ends_at) == :lt
+  end
+
+  defp exact_instants?(_starts_at, _ends_at), do: false
+
+  defp date_only(date) do
+    result(date, :date_only, nil, nil, nil, nil, "date_only")
+  end
+
+  defp stored_period(date, period) do
+    result(date, :period, period, nil, nil, nil, "stored_period")
+  end
+
+  defp exact(date, starts_at, ends_at) do
+    result(date, :exact, nil, starts_at, ends_at, starts_at.time_zone, "exact_source")
+  end
+
+  defp result(date, precision, period, starts_at, ends_at, time_zone, policy) do
+    %{
+      source_date: date,
+      precision: precision,
+      period: period,
+      starts_at: starts_at,
+      ends_at: ends_at,
+      time_zone: time_zone,
+      rule_version: @rule_version,
+      policy: policy
+    }
+  end
+end

defmodule ResidencySchedule.Timings.Interpreter do
  @moduledoc """
  Pure interpretation of how precisely one source occurrence states its time.

  The caller's date is kept literally; a period label never establishes hours
  and instants are only accepted as supplied, in one zone, with the end after
  the start. Nothing here reads or writes the database.
  """

  @rule_version "legacy_timing_v1"
  @periods ["AM", "PM", "Day", "Night"]

  @doc """
  Interprets stored timing facts into one precision outcome.

      iex> {:ok, result} =
      ...>   ResidencySchedule.Timings.Interpreter.interpret(%{date: ~D[2026-12-30], period: "PM"})
      iex> {result.precision, result.period, result.policy, result.starts_at}
      {:period, "PM", "stored_period", nil}

      iex> ResidencySchedule.Timings.Interpreter.interpret(%{date: ~D[2026-12-30], period: "Evening"})
      {:error, :unsupported_period}
  """
  def interpret(facts) when is_map(facts) do
    with {:ok, date} <- fetch_date(facts) do
      facts
      |> instants()
      |> interpret_shape(date, Map.get(facts, :period))
    end
  end

  def interpret(_facts), do: {:error, :invalid_date}

  defp fetch_date(%{date: %Date{} = date}), do: {:ok, date}
  defp fetch_date(_facts), do: {:error, :invalid_date}

  defp instants(facts), do: {Map.get(facts, :starts_at), Map.get(facts, :ends_at)}

  defp interpret_shape({nil, nil}, date, nil), do: {:ok, date_only(date)}

  defp interpret_shape({nil, nil}, date, period) when period in @periods,
    do: {:ok, stored_period(date, period)}

  defp interpret_shape({nil, nil}, _date, _period), do: {:error, :unsupported_period}

  defp interpret_shape({starts_at, ends_at}, date, nil) do
    if exact_instants?(starts_at, ends_at),
      do: {:ok, exact(date, starts_at, ends_at)},
      else: {:error, :invalid_instants}
  end

  defp interpret_shape(_instants, _date, _period), do: {:error, :invalid_instants}

  defp exact_instants?(%DateTime{} = starts_at, %DateTime{} = ends_at) do
    starts_at.time_zone == ends_at.time_zone and DateTime.compare(starts_at, ends_at) == :lt
  end

  defp exact_instants?(_starts_at, _ends_at), do: false

  defp date_only(date) do
    result(date, :date_only, nil, nil, nil, nil, "date_only")
  end

  defp stored_period(date, period) do
    result(date, :period, period, nil, nil, nil, "stored_period")
  end

  defp exact(date, starts_at, ends_at) do
    result(date, :exact, nil, starts_at, ends_at, starts_at.time_zone, "exact_source")
  end

  defp result(date, precision, period, starts_at, ends_at, time_zone, policy) do
    %{
      source_date: date,
      precision: precision,
      period: period,
      starts_at: starts_at,
      ends_at: ends_at,
      time_zone: time_zone,
      rule_version: @rule_version,
      policy: policy
    }
  end
end

defmodule ResidencySchedule.Timings.Backfill do
  @moduledoc false
  import Ecto.Query

  alias ResidencySchedule.DetailedSchedules.{Activity, ActivitySource, ImportBatch}
  alias ResidencySchedule.Repo
  alias ResidencySchedule.ScheduleCache.Revision
  alias ResidencySchedule.Timings.{Interpreter, Timing}

  @rule_version "legacy_timing_v1"

  @doc """
  Records missing timing precision for saved sources from stored facts only.

      iex> _ctx = ResidencySchedule.TimingDoctestFixtures.source()
      iex> {:ok, counts} = ResidencySchedule.Timings.Backfill.run(batch_size: 1)
      iex> {counts.processed, counts.period, counts.conflicting}
      {1, 1, 0}
  """
  def run(options) do
    with {:ok, size} <- batch_size(options) do
      fill_pages(0, size, counts())
    end
  end

  defp counts do
    %{processed: 0, period: 0, date_only: 0, unchanged: 0, conflicting: 0}
  end

  defp batch_size(options) when is_list(options) do
    if Keyword.keyword?(options) and Enum.all?(Keyword.keys(options), &(&1 == :batch_size)) do
      case Keyword.get(options, :batch_size, 500) do
        size when is_integer(size) and size in 1..1000 -> {:ok, size}
        _ -> {:error, :invalid_batch_size}
      end
    else
      {:error, :invalid_batch_size}
    end
  end

  defp batch_size(_options), do: {:error, :invalid_batch_size}

  defp fill_pages(after_id, size, total) do
    ids =
      ActivitySource
      |> where([source], source.id > ^after_id)
      |> order_by([source], source.id)
      |> limit(^size)
      |> select([source], source.id)
      |> Repo.all()

    case ids do
      [] -> {:ok, total}
      _ -> fill_next(ids, size, total)
    end
  end

  defp fill_next(ids, size, total) do
    case Repo.transaction(fn -> fill_page(ids) end) do
      {:ok, page} ->
        updated = Map.merge(total, page, fn _key, previous, value -> previous + value end)
        fill_pages(List.last(ids), size, updated)

      {:error, reason} ->
        {:error, reason}
    end
  end

  defp fill_page(ids) do
    Revision.lock()

    ids
    |> source_rows()
    |> Enum.reduce(counts(), &fill_source/2)
  end

  defp source_rows(ids) do
    from(source in ActivitySource,
      join: activity in Activity,
      on: activity.id == source.activity_id,
      join: batch in ImportBatch,
      on: batch.id == source.batch_id,
      where: source.id in ^ids,
      order_by: source.id,
      lock: "FOR UPDATE",
      select: %{source: source, activity: activity, batch: batch}
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp fill_source(row, totals) do
    namespace = validate_namespace(row.batch)

    existing =
      Timing
      |> where([timing], timing.original_source_id == ^row.source.id)
      |> lock("FOR UPDATE")
      |> Repo.one()

    cond do
      is_nil(existing) -> fill_missing(row, namespace, totals)
      existing.evidence_origin != "legacy_code" -> increment(totals, :unchanged)
      true -> retained_result(existing, row, totals)
    end
  end

  defp validate_namespace(%ImportBatch{source_kind: kind}) when kind in ["csv", "qgenda"],
    do: kind

  defp validate_namespace(_batch), do: Repo.rollback(:unsupported_namespace)

  defp retained_result(existing, row, totals) do
    if existing.rule_version == @rule_version and
         existing.input_digest == input_digest(source_snapshot(row.activity)),
       do: increment(totals, :unchanged),
       else: increment(totals, :conflicting)
  end

  defp fill_missing(row, namespace, totals) do
    case Interpreter.interpret(%{date: row.activity.date, period: row.activity.period}) do
      {:ok, result} ->
        insert_timing(row, namespace, result)
        totals |> increment(:processed) |> increment(result.precision)

      {:error, :unsupported_period} ->
        increment(totals, :conflicting)
    end
  end

  defp insert_timing(row, namespace, result) do
    snapshot = source_snapshot(row.activity)

    Repo.insert!(%Timing{
      original_source_id: row.source.id,
      activity_source_id: row.source.id,
      namespace: namespace,
      source_date: result.source_date,
      precision: Atom.to_string(result.precision),
      period: result.period,
      starts_at: result.starts_at,
      ends_at: result.ends_at,
      time_zone: result.time_zone,
      source_snapshot: snapshot,
      input_digest: input_digest(snapshot),
      rule_version: result.rule_version,
      policy: result.policy,
      evidence_origin: "legacy_code"
    })
  end

  defp source_snapshot(%Activity{} = activity) do
    %{
      "date" => Date.to_iso8601(activity.date),
      "raw_task" => activity.raw_task,
      "period" => activity.period
    }
  end

  defp input_digest(snapshot) do
    {snapshot, @rule_version}
    |> :erlang.term_to_binary([:deterministic])
    |> then(&:crypto.hash(:sha256, &1))
    |> Base.encode16(case: :lower)
  end

  defp increment(counts, key), do: Map.update!(counts, key, &(&1 + 1))
end

+++ b/test/support/migration_doctests.ex
@@ -0,0 +1,61 @@
+defmodule ResidencySchedule.MigrationDoctests do
+  @moduledoc """
+  Compiles migrations under `priv/repo/migrations/` so their modules can be
+  tested and doctested.
+
+  Migrations are not on the compile path. `Code.require_file/1` loads them in
+  memory, but `doctest` and `Code.fetch_docs/1` read documentation from a beam
+  on the code path, and `mix test` compiles with `docs: false`. This module
+  compiles each matching file with docs, writes its beam into a test-only
+  directory under the build path and adds that directory to the code path.
+
+  It runs once from `test/test_helper.exs`, before any test file is loaded, so
+  the same module is never required or compiled twice concurrently by
+  separate test files.
+  """
+
+  @doc """
+  Compiles every migration matching `glob` (relative to the project root) into
+  `Mix.Project.build_path()/migration_doctests` and adds that directory to the
+  code path. Returns the list of compiled modules.
+
+  The `:ignore_module_conflict` and `:docs` compiler options are set for the
+  compilation only and restored afterwards. Each beam is written to a temporary
+  name and renamed into place so a concurrent partition never reads a partial
+  file.
+  """
+  def compile!(glob) do
+    beam_dir = Path.join(Mix.Project.build_path(), "migration_doctests")
+    File.mkdir_p!(beam_dir)
+
+    modules =
+      with_compiler_options([ignore_module_conflict: true, docs: true], fn ->
+        for path <- Path.wildcard(glob),
+            {module, binary} <- Code.compile_file(path) do
+          write_beam(beam_dir, module, binary)
+          module
+        end
+      end)
+
+    true = Code.append_path(beam_dir)
+    modules
+  end
+
+  defp with_compiler_options(options, fun) do
+    previous = for {key, _value} <- options, do: {key, Code.get_compiler_option(key)}
+    for {key, value} <- options, do: Code.put_compiler_option(key, value)
+
+    try do
+      fun.()
+    after
+      for {key, value} <- previous, do: Code.put_compiler_option(key, value)
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp write_beam(beam_dir, module, binary) do
+    beam = Path.join(beam_dir, "#{module}.beam")
+    temporary = "#{beam}.#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}.tmp"
+    File.write!(temporary, binary)
+    File.rename!(temporary, beam)
+  end
+end

    |> Enum.map(fn [block] ->

        |> Map.new(fn line ->

      %{

        dtstart: props["DTSTART"],
        dtend: props["DTEND"],
        summary: props["SUMMARY"]
      }
    end)

defmodule ResidencySchedule.EffectiveSchedule.ComparisonTest do
  use ResidencySchedule.DataCase, async: true

  alias ResidencySchedule.EffectiveSchedule
  alias ResidencySchedule.EffectiveSchedule.Comparison
  alias ResidencySchedule.ScheduleFixtures

  doctest Comparison

    %{
      person_id: schedule_resident_id * 10,
      schedule_resident_id: schedule_resident_id,
      schedule_id: 1,
      date: date,
      duties: duties,
      off: if(duties == [], do: :blank, else: nil)
    }
  end

    %{
      kind: :rotation,
      code: code,
      label: code,
      status: :working,
      source_tasks: [],
      timing: %{precision: :date_only, period: nil},
      covered_by_person_id: nil,
      original_person_id: nil,
      source_assignment_date: nil
    }
  end

  defp event(uid, dtstart) do
    %{uid: uid, dtstart: dtstart, dtend: dtstart, summary: "Ambulatory"}
  end

  describe "diff_days/2" do
    test "identical record sets differ nowhere" do
      records = [
        record(1, ~D[2026-07-06], [duty("ambulatory")]),
        record(1, ~D[2026-07-07]),
        record(2, ~D[2026-07-06], [duty("oncology")])
      ]

      assert Comparison.diff_days(records, records) == {3, []}
      assert Comparison.diff_days([], []) == {0, []}
    end

    test "a record that differs on either side is listed with both versions" do
      same = record(1, ~D[2026-07-06], [duty("ambulatory")])
      legacy = record(1, ~D[2026-07-07], [duty("ambulatory")])
      v2 = record(1, ~D[2026-07-07], [duty("elective")])

      assert Comparison.diff_days([same, legacy], [same, v2]) ==
               {1, [%{schedule_resident_id: 1, date: ~D[2026-07-07], legacy: legacy, v2: v2}]}
    end

    test "a day present on only one side is listed with nil for the other" do
      same = record(2, ~D[2026-07-06])
      only_legacy = record(1, ~D[2026-07-06])
      only_v2 = record(3, ~D[2026-07-08])

      assert Comparison.diff_days([only_legacy, same], [same, only_v2]) ==
               {1,
                [
                  %{schedule_resident_id: 1, date: ~D[2026-07-06], legacy: only_legacy, v2: nil},
                  %{schedule_resident_id: 3, date: ~D[2026-07-08], legacy: nil, v2: only_v2}
                ]}
    end

    test "differing days are sorted by resident then chronological date" do
      records = [
        record(2, ~D[2026-01-05]),
        record(2, ~D[2025-12-31]),
        record(1, ~D[2026-07-06])
      ]

      {0, differing} = Comparison.diff_days(records, [])

      assert Enum.map(differing, &{&1.schedule_resident_id, &1.date}) == [
               {1, ~D[2026-07-06]},
               {2, ~D[2025-12-31]},
               {2, ~D[2026-01-05]}
             ]
    end
  end

  describe "diff_events/2" do
    test "identical per-person sets differ nowhere" do
      events = %{
        5 => [event("seg-ambulatory-2026-07-06-2026-07-06@residency-schedule", "20260706T060000")],
        6 => []
      }

      assert Comparison.diff_events(events, events) == []
      assert Comparison.diff_events(%{}, %{}) == []
    end

    test "events on only one side are listed per person with nil for the other" do
      shared = event("seg-ambulatory-2026-07-06-2026-07-06@residency-schedule", "20260706T060000")
      legacy_only = event("seg-ambulatory-2026-07-06-2026-07-07@residency-schedule", "20260707T060000")
      v2_only = event("seg-elective-2026-07-06-2026-07-07@residency-schedule", "20260707T060000")
      missing_person = event("seg-vacation-2026-07-08@residency-schedule", "20260708")

      legacy = %{5 => [shared, legacy_only], 6 => [missing_person]}
      v2 = %{5 => [v2_only, shared]}

      assert Comparison.diff_events(legacy, v2) == [
               %{person_id: 5, legacy: legacy_only, v2: nil},
               %{person_id: 5, legacy: nil, v2: v2_only},
               %{person_id: 6, legacy: missing_person, v2: nil}
             ]
    end

    test "a changed summary or end on the same uid counts as one event on each side" do
      before = event("seg-ambulatory-2026-07-06-2026-07-06@residency-schedule", "20260706T060000")
      changed = %{before | summary: "Elective"}

      assert Comparison.diff_events(%{5 => [before]}, %{5 => [changed]}) == [
               %{person_id: 5, legacy: before, v2: nil},
               %{person_id: 5, legacy: nil, v2: changed}
             ]
    end

    test "order of events within a person does not matter" do
      first = event("seg-ambulatory-2026-07-06-2026-07-06@residency-schedule", "20260706T060000")
      second = event("seg-ambulatory-2026-07-06-2026-07-07@residency-schedule", "20260707T060000")
      assert Comparison.diff_events(%{5 => [first, second]}, %{5 => [second, first]}) == []
    end
  end

  describe "run/1" do
    test "reports zero differences and every record identical for a seeded schedule" do
      %{schedule: schedule} = ScheduleFixtures.seed_mini_schedule()
      {:ok, records} = EffectiveSchedule.for_schedule(schedule.id, :legacy)
      assert length(records) == 63

      assert Comparison.run(schedule.id) ==
               {:ok,
                %{
                  schedule_id: schedule.id,
                  identical_days: 63,
                  differing_days: 0,
                  differing_calendar_events: 0,
                  differing_consumer_outputs: 0,
                  detail: %{days: [], calendar_events: []}
                }}
    end

    test "covers overrides and other schedules of the same people without differences" do
      data = ScheduleFixtures.seed_mini_schedule()
      ScheduleFixtures.seed_prior_year_for_clare(data)
      rotation = ScheduleFixtures.rotation_on(data.mary, ~D[2026-07-14])

      {:ok, _} =
        ResidencySchedule.ShiftOverrides.create_override(%{
          rotation_id: rotation.id,
          covering_schedule_resident_id: data.tiff.id,
          override_start_date: ~D[2026-07-15],
          override_end_date: ~D[2026-07-16]
        })

      assert {:ok, summary} = Comparison.run(data.schedule.id)
      assert summary.identical_days == 63
      assert summary.differing_days == 0
      assert summary.differing_calendar_events == 0
      assert summary.detail == %{days: [], calendar_events: []}
    end

    test "an unknown schedule is :not_found" do
      assert Comparison.run(-1) == {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end
end

--- /dev/null
+++ b/lib/residency_schedule/effective_schedule.ex
@@ -0,0 +1,112 @@
+defmodule ResidencySchedule.EffectiveSchedule do
+  @moduledoc """
+  Computes schedule meaning as daily duty records and calendar identity sets.
+
+  The fixed interface of plan D2. `version` selects the computation: `:legacy`
+  adapts the existing projection paths; `:v2` currently routes to the same
+  adapter and will be replaced by the new computation in the next step.
+  """
+
+  alias ResidencySchedule.EffectiveSchedule.LegacyAdapter
+  alias ResidencySchedule.Ical
+  alias ResidencySchedule.Residents
+  alias ResidencySchedule.Rotations
+  alias ResidencySchedule.Schedules
+
+  @versions [:legacy, :v2]
+
+  @doc """
+  Daily records for every membership of a schedule, sorted by schedule
+  resident then date. Returns `{:error, :not_found}` for an unknown schedule
+  and `{:error, :unknown_version}` for a version other than `:legacy` or `:v2`.
+
+  Exempt from doctest — hits the database. See `EffectiveScheduleTest`.
+  """
+  def for_schedule(schedule_id, version) do
+    with :ok <- validate_version(version),
+         {:ok, schedule} <- fetch_schedule(schedule_id) do
+      {:ok, schedule_records(schedule.id, version)}
+    end
+  end
+
+  @doc """
+  Daily records for every schedule appearance of a person, sorted by schedule
+  then date. An unknown person has no records.
+
+  Exempt from doctest — hits the database. See `EffectiveScheduleTest`.
+  """
+  def for_person(person_id, version) do
+    with :ok <- validate_version(version) do
+      {:ok, person_records(person_id, version)}
+    end
+  end
+
+  @doc """
+  Daily records for one date of a schedule, one per membership.
+
+  Exempt from doctest — hits the database. See `EffectiveScheduleTest`.
+  """
+  def for_date(schedule_id, date, version) do
+    with {:ok, records} <- for_schedule(schedule_id, version) do
+      {:ok, Enum.filter(records, &(Date.compare(&1.date, date) == :eq))}
+    end
+  end
+
+  @doc """
+  The calendar identity set (plan D1) for every appearance of a person,
+  sorted by start then uid. An unknown person has no events.
+
+  Exempt from doctest — hits the database. See `EffectiveScheduleTest`.
+  """
+  def calendar_events(person_id, version) do
+    with :ok <- validate_version(version) do
+      {:ok, person_events(person_id, version)}
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp validate_version(version) when version in @versions, do: :ok
+  defp validate_version(_version), do: {:error, :unknown_version}
+
+  defp fetch_schedule(schedule_id) do
+    case Schedules.get_schedule(schedule_id) do
+      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
+      schedule -> {:ok, schedule}
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp schedule_records(schedule_id, :legacy),
+    do: LegacyAdapter.daily_records_for_schedule(schedule_id)
+
+  defp schedule_records(schedule_id, :v2),
+    do: LegacyAdapter.daily_records_for_schedule(schedule_id)
+
+  defp person_records(person_id, version) do
+    person_id
+    |> Residents.list_appearances_for_person()
+    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.schedule_id)
+    |> Enum.flat_map(&appearance_records(&1, version))
+  end
+
+  defp appearance_records(appearance, version) do
+    appearance.schedule_id
+    |> schedule_records(version)
+    |> Enum.filter(&(&1.schedule_resident_id == appearance.id))
+  end
+
+  defp person_events(person_id, :legacy), do: legacy_person_events(person_id)
+  defp person_events(person_id, :v2), do: legacy_person_events(person_id)
+
+  defp legacy_person_events(person_id) do
+    person_id
+    |> Rotations.effective_segments_for_person()
+    |> Ical.events_from_segments(person_name(person_id))
+    |> Enum.sort_by(&{&1.dtstart, &1.uid})
+  end
+
+  defp person_name(person_id) do
+    case Residents.list_appearances_for_person(person_id) do
+      [] -> ""
+      [appearance | _] -> appearance.name
+    end
+  end
+end

+defmodule ResidencySchedule.EffectiveSchedule.Comparison do
+  @moduledoc """
+  Compares the `:legacy` and `:v2` effective-schedule reads of one schedule.
+
+  Results are returned in memory only (plan D5): nothing is persisted, logged
+  or written to a file. Telemetry receives only the aggregate mismatch count.
+  """
+
+  alias ResidencySchedule.EffectiveSchedule
+  alias ResidencySchedule.Observability.Tracing
+
+  @doc """
+  Runs the comparison for a schedule and returns aggregate counts with the
+  differing records as detail. Returns `{:error, :not_found}` for an unknown
+  schedule.
+
+  Exempt from doctest — hits the database. See `ComparisonTest`.
+  """
+  def run(schedule_id) do
+    Tracing.phase(:schedule_compare, fn -> compare_schedule(schedule_id) end)
+  end
+
+  @doc """
+  Diffs two daily record lists keyed by schedule resident and date.
+
+  Returns the number of identical records and the differing days, sorted by
+  schedule resident then chronological date, each with both versions (nil
+  when a side has no record).
+
+      iex> alias ResidencySchedule.EffectiveSchedule.Comparison
+      iex> legacy = %{schedule_resident_id: 1, date: ~D[2026-07-06], duties: [], off: :blank}
+      iex> v2 = %{legacy | off: :vacation}
+      iex> Comparison.diff_days([legacy], [v2])
+      {0, [%{schedule_resident_id: 1, date: ~D[2026-07-06], legacy: legacy, v2: v2}]}
+
+      iex> alias ResidencySchedule.EffectiveSchedule.Comparison
+      iex> record = %{schedule_resident_id: 1, date: ~D[2026-07-06], duties: [], off: :blank}
+      iex> Comparison.diff_days([record], [record])
+      {1, []}
+  """
+  def diff_days(legacy, v2) do
+    legacy_by_key = index_days(legacy)
+    v2_by_key = index_days(v2)
+
+    legacy_by_key
+    |> Map.keys()
+    |> Enum.concat(Map.keys(v2_by_key))
+    |> Enum.uniq()
+    |> Enum.sort_by(fn {resident_id, date} -> {resident_id, Date.to_gregorian_days(date)} end)
+    |> Enum.reduce({0, []}, &collect_day(&1, legacy_by_key, v2_by_key, &2))
+    |> reverse_differing()
+  end
+
+  @doc """
+  Diffs calendar identity sets keyed by person. Returns one entry per event
+  present on only one side, ordered by person then legacy-only before v2-only.
+
+      iex> alias ResidencySchedule.EffectiveSchedule.Comparison
+      iex> event = %{uid: "seg-vacation-2026-07-06@residency-schedule", dtstart: "20260706", dtend: "20260707", summary: "Vacation"}

defmodule ResidencySchedule.EffectiveSchedule do
  @moduledoc """
  Computes schedule meaning as daily duty records and calendar identity sets.

  The fixed interface of plan D2. `version` selects the computation: `:legacy`
  adapts the existing projection paths; `:v2` currently routes to the same
  adapter and will be replaced by the new computation in the next step.
  """

  alias ResidencySchedule.EffectiveSchedule.LegacyAdapter
  alias ResidencySchedule.Ical
  alias ResidencySchedule.Residents
  alias ResidencySchedule.Rotations
  alias ResidencySchedule.Schedules

  @versions [:legacy, :v2]

  @doc """
  Daily records for every membership of a schedule, sorted by schedule
  resident then date. Returns `{:error, :not_found}` for an unknown schedule
  and `{:error, :unknown_version}` for a version other than `:legacy` or `:v2`.

  Exempt from doctest — hits the database. See `EffectiveScheduleTest`.
  """
  def for_schedule(schedule_id, version) do
    with :ok <- validate_version(version),
         {:ok, schedule} <- fetch_schedule(schedule_id) do
      {:ok, schedule_records(schedule.id, version)}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Daily records for every schedule appearance of a person, sorted by schedule
  then date. An unknown person has no records.

  Exempt from doctest — hits the database. See `EffectiveScheduleTest`.
  """
  def for_person(person_id, version) do
    with :ok <- validate_version(version) do
      {:ok, person_records(person_id, version)}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Daily records for one date of a schedule, one per membership.

  Exempt from doctest — hits the database. See `EffectiveScheduleTest`.
  """
  def for_date(schedule_id, date, version) do
    with {:ok, records} <- for_schedule(schedule_id, version) do
      {:ok, Enum.filter(records, &(Date.compare(&1.date, date) == :eq))}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  The calendar identity set (plan D1) for every appearance of a person,
  sorted by start then uid. An unknown person has no events.

  Exempt from doctest — hits the database. See `EffectiveScheduleTest`.
  """
  def calendar_events(person_id, version) do
    with :ok <- validate_version(version) do
      {:ok, person_events(person_id, version)}
    end
  end

  defp validate_version(version) when version in @versions, do: :ok
  defp validate_version(_version), do: {:error, :unknown_version}

  defp fetch_schedule(schedule_id) do
    case Schedules.get_schedule(schedule_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
      schedule -> {:ok, schedule}
    end
  end

  defp schedule_records(schedule_id, :legacy),
    do: LegacyAdapter.daily_records_for_schedule(schedule_id)

  defp schedule_records(schedule_id, :v2),
    do: LegacyAdapter.daily_records_for_schedule(schedule_id)

  defp person_records(person_id, version) do
    person_id
    |> Residents.list_appearances_for_person()
    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.schedule_id)
    |> Enum.flat_map(&appearance_records(&1, version))
  end

    |> schedule_records(version)
    |> Enum.filter(&(&1.schedule_resident_id == appearance.id))
  end

  defp person_events(person_id, :legacy), do: legacy_person_events(person_id)
  defp person_events(person_id, :v2), do: legacy_person_events(person_id)

  defp legacy_person_events(person_id) do
    person_id
    |> Rotations.effective_segments_for_person()
    |> Ical.events_from_segments(person_name(person_id))
    |> Enum.sort_by(&{&1.dtstart, &1.uid})
  end

  defp person_name(person_id) do
    case Residents.list_appearances_for_person(person_id) do
      [] -> ""
      [appearance | _] -> appearance.name
    end
  end
end

defmodule ResidencySchedule.EffectiveSchedule.Comparison do
  @moduledoc """
  Compares the `:legacy` and `:v2` effective-schedule reads of one schedule.

  Results are returned in memory only (plan D5): nothing is persisted, logged
  or written to a file. Telemetry receives only the aggregate mismatch count.
  """

  alias ResidencySchedule.EffectiveSchedule
  alias ResidencySchedule.Observability.Tracing

  @doc """
  Runs the comparison for a schedule and returns aggregate counts with the
  differing records as detail. Returns `{:error, :not_found}` for an unknown
  schedule.

  Exempt from doctest — hits the database. See `ComparisonTest`.
  """
  def run(schedule_id) do
    Tracing.phase(:schedule_compare, fn -> compare_schedule(schedule_id) end)
  end

  @doc """
  Diffs two daily record lists keyed by schedule resident and date.

  Returns the number of identical records and the differing days, sorted by
  schedule resident then chronological date, each with both versions (nil
  when a side has no record).

      iex> alias ResidencySchedule.EffectiveSchedule.Comparison
      iex> legacy = %{schedule_resident_id: 1, date: ~D[2026-07-06], duties: [], off: :blank}
      iex> v2 = %{legacy | off: :vacation}
      iex> Comparison.diff_days([legacy], [v2])
      {0, [%{schedule_resident_id: 1, date: ~D[2026-07-06], legacy: legacy, v2: v2}]}

      iex> alias ResidencySchedule.EffectiveSchedule.Comparison
      iex> record = %{schedule_resident_id: 1, date: ~D[2026-07-06], duties: [], off: :blank}
      iex> Comparison.diff_days([record], [record])
      {1, []}
  """
  def diff_days(legacy, v2) do
    legacy_by_key = index_days(legacy)
    v2_by_key = index_days(v2)

    legacy_by_key
    |> Map.keys()
    |> Enum.concat(Map.keys(v2_by_key))
    |> Enum.uniq()
    |> Enum.sort_by(fn {resident_id, date} -> {resident_id, Date.to_gregorian_days(date)} end)
    |> Enum.reduce({0, []}, &collect_day(&1, legacy_by_key, v2_by_key, &2))
    |> reverse_differing()
  end

  @doc """
  Diffs calendar identity sets keyed by person. Returns one entry per event
  present on only one side, ordered by person then legacy-only before v2-only.

      iex> alias ResidencySchedule.EffectiveSchedule.Comparison
      iex> event = %{uid: "seg-vacation-2026-07-06@residency-schedule", dtstart: "20260706", dtend: "20260707", summary: "Vacation"}
      iex> Comparison.diff_events(%{5 => [event]}, %{5 => []})
      [%{person_id: 5, legacy: event, v2: nil}]

      iex> alias ResidencySchedule.EffectiveSchedule.Comparison
      iex> event = %{uid: "seg-vacation-2026-07-06@residency-schedule", dtstart: "20260706", dtend: "20260707", summary: "Vacation"}
      iex> Comparison.diff_events(%{5 => [event]}, %{5 => [event]})
      []
  """
  def diff_events(legacy, v2) do
    legacy
    |> Map.keys()
    |> Enum.concat(Map.keys(v2))
    |> Enum.uniq()
    |> Enum.sort()
    |> Enum.flat_map(&person_event_differences(&1, legacy, v2))
  end

  defp compare_schedule(schedule_id) do
    with {:ok, legacy} <- EffectiveSchedule.for_schedule(schedule_id, :legacy),
         {:ok, v2} <- EffectiveSchedule.for_schedule(schedule_id, :v2) do
      {:ok, build_summary(schedule_id, legacy, v2)}
    end
  end

  defp build_summary(schedule_id, legacy, v2) do
    {identical_days, differing_days} = diff_days(legacy, v2)
    differing_events = diff_events(person_events(legacy, :legacy), person_events(v2, :v2))
    Tracing.count(:mismatches, length(differing_days) + length(differing_events))

    %{
      schedule_id: schedule_id,
      identical_days: identical_days,
      differing_days: length(differing_days),
      differing_calendar_events: length(differing_events),
      differing_consumer_outputs: 0,
      detail: %{days: differing_days, calendar_events: differing_events}
    }
  end

  defp person_events(records, version) do
    records
    |> Enum.map(& &1.person_id)
    |> Enum.uniq()
    |> Map.new(&{&1, calendar_events(&1, version)})
  end

  defp calendar_events(person_id, version) do
    {:ok, events} = EffectiveSchedule.calendar_events(person_id, version)
    events
  end

  defp index_days(records), do: Map.new(records, &{{&1.schedule_resident_id, &1.date}, &1})

  defp collect_day({resident_id, date} = key, legacy_by_key, v2_by_key, {identical, differing}) do
    legacy = Map.get(legacy_by_key, key)
    v2 = Map.get(v2_by_key, key)

    if legacy == v2 do
      {identical + 1, differing}
    else
      {identical,
       [%{schedule_resident_id: resident_id, date: date, legacy: legacy, v2: v2} | differing]}
    end
  end

  defp reverse_differing({identical, differing}), do: {identical, Enum.reverse(differing)}

  defp person_event_differences(person_id, legacy, v2) do
    legacy_events = Map.get(legacy, person_id, [])
    v2_events = Map.get(v2, person_id, [])

    only_in(legacy_events, v2_events, &%{person_id: person_id, legacy: &1, v2: nil}) ++
      only_in(v2_events, legacy_events, &%{person_id: person_id, legacy: nil, v2: &1})
  end

  defp only_in(events, others, build) do
    others = MapSet.new(others)

    events
    |> Enum.reject(&MapSet.member?(others, &1))
    |> Enum.map(build)
  end
end

+defmodule ResidencySchedule.Repo.Migrations.RunPhase2Backfills do
+  @moduledoc """
+  Runs the four Phase 2 backfills once during `ResidencySchedule.Release.migrate/0`.
+
+  The migration is one-shot, idempotent and additive: it fills empty QGenda
+  source references, observes resident identity keys, seeds the legacy task
+  facts and classifies saved occurrences, then records timing precision. It
+  never updates or deletes an existing backfilled row, so rerunning the matching
+  `ResidencySchedule.Release.backfill_*` command afterwards is the documented
+  verification and reports zero new rows.
+
+  The DDL transaction and migration lock are disabled because each backfill
+  already commits one bounded transaction per batch under its own write lock.
+  Wrapping every batch in a single outer transaction would hold the migration
+  lock for the whole run, make the earlier completed batches roll back on a
+  later failure, and remove the "interrupted work can be rerun" guarantee the
+  backfills provide. A step failure still stops `Release.migrate/0`.
+
+  `up/0` honours the `:run_phase2_backfills_on_migrate` application setting
+  (default `true`, `false` in `config/test.exs`), so test databases are never
+  seeded by migration; the test suite seeds per sandbox instead. `run/0` ignores
+  the flag.
+  """
+  use Ecto.Migration
+
+  require Logger
+
+  alias ResidencySchedule.{IdentityMappings, SourceProvenance, TaskMappings, Timings}
+
+  @disable_ddl_transaction true
+  @disable_migration_lock true
+
+  def up do
+    if Application.get_env(:residency_schedule, :run_phase2_backfills_on_migrate, true) do
+      run_or_raise()
+    else
+      Logger.info("Phase 2 backfill skipped: run_phase2_backfills_on_migrate is false")
+      :ok
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp run_or_raise do
+    case run() do
+      {:ok, _counts} ->
+        :ok
+
+      {:error, {step, reason}} ->
+        raise "Phase 2 backfill failed: #{inspect(step)} #{inspect(reason)}"
+    end
+  end
+
+  def down, do: :ok
+
+  @doc """
+  Executes the backfills in order, stopping at the first failing step.
+
+  Returns the counts of every step, or `{:error, {step, reason}}` for the step
+  that failed. Only aggregate counts are logged.
+
+      iex> _ctx = ResidencySchedule.TimingDoctestFixtures.source()
+      iex> {:ok, result} = ResidencySchedule.Repo.Migrations.RunPhase2Backfills.run()
+      iex> {result.timings.processed, result.task_classifications.classifications.resolved}
+      {1, 1}
+  """
+  def run do
+    with {:ok, provenance} <- step(:source_provenance, &SourceProvenance.backfill/0),
+         {:ok, identities} <- step(:identity_mappings, &IdentityMappings.backfill/0),
+         {:ok, classifications} <- step(:task_classifications, &classify_tasks/0),
+         {:ok, timings} <- step(:timings, &Timings.backfill/0) do
+      {:ok,
+       %{
+         source_provenance: provenance,
+         identity_mappings: identities,
+         task_classifications: classifications,
+         timings: timings
+       }}
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp classify_tasks do
+    with {:ok, seed} <- TaskMappings.seed_legacy(),
+         {:ok, classifications} <- TaskMappings.backfill() do
+      {:ok, %{seed: seed, classifications: classifications}}
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp step(name, backfill) do
+    case backfill.() do
+      {:ok, counts} ->
+        Logger.info("Phase 2 backfill #{name} completed: #{inspect(counts)}")
+        {:ok, counts}
+
+      {:error, reason} ->
+        Logger.info("Phase 2 backfill #{name} failed")
+        {:error, {name, reason}}
+    end
+  end

+defmodule ResidencySchedule.MigrationDoctests do
+  @moduledoc """
+  Compiles migrations under `priv/repo/migrations/` so their modules can be
+  tested and doctested.
+
+  Migrations are not on the compile path. `Code.require_file/1` loads them in
+  memory, but `doctest` and `Code.fetch_docs/1` read documentation from a beam
+  on the code path, and `mix test` compiles with `docs: false`. This module
+  compiles each matching file with docs, writes its beam into a test-only
+  directory under the build path and adds that directory to the code path.
+
+  It runs once from `test/test_helper.exs`, before any test file is loaded, so
+  the same module is never required or compiled twice concurrently by
+  separate test files.
+  """
+
+  @doc """
+  Compiles every migration matching `glob` (relative to the project root) into
+  `Mix.Project.build_path()/migration_doctests` and adds that directory to the
+  code path. Returns the list of compiled modules.
+
+  The `:ignore_module_conflict` and `:docs` compiler options are set for the
+  compilation only and restored afterwards. Each beam is written to a temporary
+  name and renamed into place so a concurrent partition never reads a partial
+  file.
+  """
+  def compile!(glob) do
+    beam_dir = Path.join(Mix.Project.build_path(), "migration_doctests")
+    File.mkdir_p!(beam_dir)
+
+    modules =
+      with_compiler_options([ignore_module_conflict: true, docs: true], fn ->
+        for path <- Path.wildcard(glob),
+            {module, binary} <- Code.compile_file(path) do
+          write_beam(beam_dir, module, binary)
+          module
+        end
+      end)
+
+    true = Code.append_path(beam_dir)
+    modules
+  end
+
+  defp with_compiler_options(options, fun) do
+    previous = for {key, _value} <- options, do: {key, Code.get_compiler_option(key)}
+    for {key, value} <- options, do: Code.put_compiler_option(key, value)
+
+    try do
+      fun.()
+    after
+      for {key, value} <- previous, do: Code.put_compiler_option(key, value)
+    end
+  end
+
+  defp write_beam(beam_dir, module, binary) do
+    beam = Path.join(beam_dir, "#{module}.beam")
+    temporary = "#{beam}.#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}.tmp"
+    File.write!(temporary, binary)
+    File.rename!(temporary, beam)
+  end
+end

+defmodule ResidencySchedule.EffectiveScheduleV2Fixtures do
+  @moduledoc "Synthetic retained Phase 2 evidence for effective-read contracts."
+
+  alias ResidencySchedule.{IdentityMappings, Repo, Residents, ScheduleFixtures, Schedules, TaskMappings, Timings}
+  alias ResidencySchedule.DetailedSchedules.{Activity, ActivitySource, ImportBatch}
+  alias ResidencySchedule.Rotations.Rotation
+  alias ResidencySchedule.TaskMappings.Classification
+  alias ResidencySchedule.Timings.Timing
+
+  @doc "Creates an isolated synthetic membership. Database fixture; exempt from doctest."
+  def member(year \\ 2026, number \\ 1) do
+    {:ok, schedule} = Schedules.upsert_schedule(year, "#{year}–#{year + 1}")
+    {:ok, member} = Residents.insert_resident(schedule.id, %{
+      name: "Synthetic Resident #{number}", position_code: "R2-#{number}",
+      residency_year: 2, schedule_number: number
+    })
+    member
+  end
+
+  @doc "Creates a stored baseline block. Database fixture; exempt from doctest."
+  def rotation(member, type, first, last, slot \\ 0) do
+    Repo.insert!(%Rotation{schedule_resident_id: member.id, rotation_type: type,
+      start_date: first, end_date: last, slot_index: slot})
+  end
+
+  @doc "Creates one literal source occurrence. Database fixture; exempt from doctest."
+  def source(member, date, task, period \\ nil) do
+    activity = Repo.insert!(%Activity{schedule_resident_id: member.id, date: date,
+      raw_task: task, period: period})
+    add_source(member, activity)
+  end
+
+  @doc "Adds another retained occurrence of an activity. Database fixture; exempt from doctest."
+  def add_source(member, activity) do
+    batch = Repo.insert!(%ImportBatch{schedule_id: member.schedule_id,
+      created_by_id: ScheduleFixtures.admin_user().id, fingerprint: Ecto.UUID.generate(),
+      header_start: activity.date, header_end: activity.date})
+    source = Repo.insert!(%ActivitySource{activity_id: activity.id, batch_id: batch.id,
+      raw_staff: "Source Alias #{member.id}", display_name: member.name, previous_name: member.name,
+      source_sheet: "Synthetic", source_cell: "A1"})
+    %{member: member, activity: activity, source: source}
+  end
+
+  @doc "Explicitly backfills and approves synthetic evidence before reads. Exempt from doctest."
+  def retain(sources, approve \\ true) do
+    {:ok, _} = TaskMappings.seed_legacy()
+    {:ok, _} = TaskMappings.backfill()
+    {:ok, _} = Timings.backfill()
+    {:ok, _} = IdentityMappings.backfill()
+    admin = ScheduleFixtures.admin_user()
+
+    sources
+    |> Enum.uniq_by(&{&1.member.id, &1.source.raw_staff})
+    |> Enum.filter(fn _ -> approve end)
+    |> Enum.each(fn %{member: member, source: source} ->
+      rows = [%{source_key: source.raw_staff, position_code: member.position_code, expected_name: member.name}]
+      {:ok, plan} = IdentityMappings.prepare_crosswalk(member.schedule_id, :qgenda, rows, admin)
+      {:ok, _} = IdentityMappings.approve_crosswalk(plan, admin)
+    end)
+    sources
+  end
+
+  @doc "Returns one retained classification. Database fixture; exempt from doctest."
+  def classification(source), do: Repo.get_by!(Classification, original_source_id: source.source.id)
+
+  @doc "Returns one retained timing. Database fixture; exempt from doctest."
+  def timing(source), do: Repo.get_by!(Timing, original_source_id: source.source.id)
+
+  @doc """
+  Builds the exact public diagnostic for an occurrence.
+
+      iex> source = %{member: %{id: 2}, activity: %{id: 3, date: ~D[2026-11-03]}, source: %{id: 4}}
+      iex> ResidencySchedule.EffectiveScheduleV2Fixtures.diagnostic(source, :missing_timing)
+      %{reason: :missing_timing, activity_id: 3, activity_source_id: 4, schedule_resident_id: 2, date: ~D[2026-11-03]}
+  """
+  def diagnostic(source, reason) do
+    %{reason: reason, activity_id: source.activity.id, activity_source_id: source.source.id,
+      schedule_resident_id: source.member.id, date: source.activity.date}
+  end
+end

+
+  @doc "Creates one literal source occurrence. Database fixture; exempt from doctest."
+  def source(member, date, task, period \\ nil) do
